summary.text: A 20-year-old woman developed headache and gastrointestinal symptoms in May 2017, followed a few days later by fever, hallucinations, disturbed consciousness and personality changes. On hospital admission, cranial MRI showed lesions in both mesial temporal lobes suspicious for herpes encephalitis, and intravenous acyclovir and prednisolone were started. She was transferred to a secondary care center, intubated because of insufficient protective reflexes, seizures and dyskinesia, and later tracheotomized.

Lumbar puncture showed lymphocytic pleocytosis, with oligoclonal bands and anti-NMDA-receptor antibodies in cerebrospinal fluid and serum, allowing the diagnosis of autoimmune limbic encephalitis; the clinical stages were typical of anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis. Viral PCR including HSV was negative. Imaging showed pulmonary embolisms and a right ovarian teratoma, which was verified by biopsy and resected.

Plasmapheresis with high-dose corticosteroids and rituximab was followed by transfer to the authors department seven weeks after onset (mRS 5, Barthel Index 0), then repeat plasmapheresis, corticosteroids, rituximab, IVIG and cyclophosphamide. With no improvement at 16 weeks, three cycles of bortezomib were given but interrupted after urinary tract infections, septic shock and CMV-associated pneumonia. Extended imaging found no neoplasia, and the left ovary removal found no occult teratoma.

Anti-NMDA receptor antibody titers stayed high and peripheral flow cytometry showed CD20 cell depletion after rituximab; daratumumab 16 mg/kg was given intravenously from 28 weeks after disease onset, 10 cycles within 13 weeks, with prednisolone, clemastine and paracetamol premedication. Over the next 2 months dyskinesia and consciousness improved and the Barthel index reached 5; she moved to intermediate care at 9 months and entered rehabilitation.

Further bortezomib cycles, continued rituximab and IVIG followed. At 18 months the tracheal cannula was removed, and nine months after daratumumab she was awake, cooperative and walking independently (Barthel index 80). At the last follow-up, 17 months after daratumumab, she cared for herself and used a smartphone but could not manage her legal matters; the last MRI showed global brain volume reduction.

Phenotyping lymphocytes before and after daratumumab treatment. Peripheral blood lymphocytes were analyzed by flow cytometry 2 days before (A,B) and 12 days after daratumumab (C) has been administered.
